title: The Friend Behind the Smile
content:
Night had quietly settled over Shimla.

The house, which had witnessed so much tension only a few hours earlier, was now wrapped in a comforting silence.

For the first time in days...

Everyone's hearts felt lighter.

Inside Yashwanth's room...

Siddu lay on the bed with his eyes open, staring at the ceiling.

A gentle smile rested on his face.

"Finally..."

"Yashwanth found the ending he deserved."

He reached for his phone, plugged in his earphones, and let his favourite playlist begin.

Soft music filled his ears.

One song after another...

Until suddenly...

A familiar English song started playing.

It was Sneha's favourite.

The smile on Siddu's face slowly disappeared.

Without wanting to...

His mind drifted back to the moments he had spent with her.

Her laughter...

Their endless conversations...

The memories he had buried deep inside his heart quietly resurfaced.

He immediately removed one earphone.

With a deep sigh, he stopped the song.

"No..."

"Not now."

He whispered to himself as he tried to push those memories away.

Just then...

The door slowly opened.

Yashwanth walked inside.

The happiness on his face hadn't faded even a little.

Seeing Siddu sitting quietly, he smiled.

"So..."

"Were you waiting for me to say 'thank you'?"

Siddu looked at him and raised an eyebrow.

"Don't even think about it."

Yashwanth laughed.

"Why?"

Siddu folded his arms with a grin.

"Because between friends..."

"There are no 'thank yous'..."

"And no 'sorrys.'"

Yashwanth burst into laughter.

"You thief!"

"You're using your own dialogue before I could."

The room echoed with their laughter.

After a few moments...

Yashwanth's smile slowly faded.

His eyes became moist.

Without saying another word...

He stepped forward and hugged Siddu tightly.

"This isn't a thank you..."

He said, his voice trembling.

"You changed my life."

"I'll never forget what you've done for me."

Tears of happiness rolled down his cheeks.

Siddu smiled warmly and gently patted his back.

"Calm down."

"I only did what a true friend should do."

They slowly pulled away from the embrace.

After wiping the tears from his eyes, Yashwanth looked at Siddu curiously.

"There is one thing I still don't understand."

"What exactly did you say to my father?"

Siddu smiled.

He leaned back in his chair before beginning.

"When I rang the doorbell..."

"Your father welcomed me warmly."

"After greeting him..."

"I told him I wanted to introduce someone."

"I introduced Varsha."

"At first..."

"He thought she was simply my friend."

"But then..."

"I told him the truth."

"I told him she wasn't there because of me."

"She was there because she loved his son."

Yashwanth listened silently.

Siddu continued.

"I told him..."

"Uncle... Yashwanth and Varsha have loved each other for a long time."

"He wanted to tell you the truth."

"But before he could gather the courage..."

"You told him that his marriage had already been fixed."

"I know he should have spoken honestly."

"But he couldn't."

"Not because he didn't trust you..."

"Because he respected you too much."

"He didn't want to hurt you."

"At the same time..."

"He couldn't stop loving Varsha."

"He wasn't choosing between you and Varsha, Uncle."

"He was trying his hardest not to lose either of you."

"I only have one request."

"Please don't misunderstand him."

"He's your son."

"He only wanted both his father and the woman he loves to remain in his life."

The room fell silent.

Yashwanth listened without blinking.

Siddu smiled softly before continuing.

"Your father didn't even think for a second."

"He smiled and said..."

"If my son had told me this even once..."

"I would have understood him."

"This is his life."

"He has every right to choose the person he wants to spend it with."

"Today..."

"I'm prouder of my son than ever before."

"Even while carrying such a heavy burden..."

"He never stopped respecting me."

Yashwanth's eyes slowly filled with tears.

"He..."

"He really said that?"

Siddu nodded with a smile.

"Every single word."

He chuckled before continuing.

"Then I noticed you walking toward the entrance."

"So I got an idea."

"I asked your father to pretend he was angry."

"I told him..."

"Uncle..."

"Please turn around with a serious face..."

"Look at Yashwanth angrily..."

"And quietly walk into your room."

Yashwanth couldn't help laughing.

"And he actually agreed?"

Siddu laughed along with him.

"He smiled and said..."

"'Alright.'"

"'Let's tease my son a little.'"

The two friends burst into laughter once again.

The fear...

The confusion...

And the countless sleepless nights...

Had finally come to an end.

Tonight...

There were no worries.

No unanswered questions.

Only two friends...

Who had stood beside each other through every storm...

Now laughing together...

Knowing that some friendships are strong enough to change destinies.
